$comment: `(_Bool)x` — THE EXPLICIT CAST, the one route to `_Bool` that did not use the truthiness chokepoint (D-CSUBSET-EXPLICIT-BOOL-CAST-IS-A-TRUNCATION). C 6.3.1.2 defines conversion of ANY scalar to `_Bool` as 'compares equal to 0', so 0 becomes false and ANY nonzero value becomes true. The DECLARATION family (`_Bool b = x;`, a call argument, a return) already realized that through `coerceCondition`, the one verb owning the truth-value vocabulary; the EXPLICIT cast fell through to a plain Cast node, and HIR->MIR's `mapCast` classifies `_Bool` as an 8-bit integer, so the pair became a WIDTH conversion — `Trunc`, which keeps only the LOW BIT. ✔MEASURED at 301e2a63 on x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows-exec AND x86_64:elf64-x86_64-linux-exec: `_Bool b = (_Bool)x;` on an `int` walls with `error[L_UnsupportedLoweringForOpcode] Trunc result: TypeKind ordinal 0 has no encoded conversion form`, so LIR's missing `_Bool`-width Trunc form was the ONLY thing between this and a silent miscompile — the instruction MIR asked for computes `(_Bool)256 == 0` where C requires 1. gcc 13.3.0 (`-std=c2x`) and clang 18.1.3 / 19 (`-std=c23`), probed SEPARATELY, all compile and run every term; gcc has no `_BitInt`, so clang is the witness for t6's two `_BitInt` rows — a missing FEATURE, not a refusal, and the disjunction still binds. ★★ EVERY VALUE IS EVEN, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN: a truncating `(_Bool)` and a correct `!= 0` AGREE on every odd value and DISAGREE on every nonzero even one, so an odd probe is vacuous — it passes on a broken build. RED-ON-DISABLE, one term per C scalar category (C 6.2.5p21, arithmetic ∪ pointer): t1 integer — 256 (low BYTE zero, so even a byte-wide Trunc says false) and 2 (low BIT zero, so even a 1-bit truncation says false); t2 floating — `0.5` is NONZERO but its integer part is 0, so any route through an integer conversion says false while C compares the VALUE with 0; t3 pointer — nothing in a pointer's low bits carries its truth value; t4 enum — projects to its underlying integer first, probed with an even nonzero enumerator; t5 a wide `__int128` whose LOW LIMB IS ENTIRELY ZERO, which a limb-0-only conversion reads as false; t6 `_BitInt` narrow (container low bit 0) and wide (bit 70 set, so limb 0 is entirely zero); t7 the cast's RESULT CONSUMED — ternary condition, arithmetic operand, and returned value — the positions that make the defect reachable from ordinary code. Each term is boolean-gated to 6 ⇒ the sum is 42 only when every one holds. Every operand is laundered through an opaque helper so the release arm exercises the runtime conversion rather than a folded constant, and each term lives in its own function so no frame grows large enough to hit the arm64 `imm9` offset limit.
